samples.summary: Whole-root JSON snapshot copies comment threads for sheet/slides/board, contradicting the "comments are never carried over" invariant
samples.evidence: `copyContent`'s JSON arm assigns *every* root key from the source snapshot onto the copy (lines 187-198). Sheet comments live inside the Yorkie root — `packages/frontend/src/app/spreadsheet/yorkie-worksheet-comments.ts:4` (`ws.comments`) and `packages/frontend/src/app/documents/document-detail.tsx:244` reads `docRoot.sheets[...].comments`. So a copied spreadsheet carries all of the source's comment threads (with their authors' user ids, names and photos), while the `doc`/`pdf` arms deliberately drop them (`readDocsRoot` only reads content/pageSetup/stylesJson). The class docstring (line 33-37) and docs/design/document-copy.md:33 both state comments are deliberately not carried over — the sheet/slides/board path violates that.

samples.summary: Snapshot round-trip demotes Yorkie Long values to 32-bit Integers, corrupting timestamps in copied roots
samples.evidence: The JSON arm writes `root[key] = value` with values that came out of `JSON.parse`, i.e. plain JS numbers. The repo documents that Yorkie 0.7.x stores any integer-valued JS number as a 32-bit Integer, which is why comment timestamps are written as bigint (`BigInt(ms) as unknown as number`) in packages/frontend/src/app/spreadsheet/yorkie-worksheet-comments.ts:8-14. Copying a sheet root therefore writes `createdAt` (~1.78e12) back as a plain number, truncating it to its low 32 bits — the copy's comment/any Long field decodes as a 1970 date. `scripts/copy-yorkie-documents.ts:115-118` (the cited precedent) has an explicit bigint branch; this implementation has none.

samples.summary: snapshotJsonRoot has no control-character fallback, so `JSON.parse(doc.toJSON())` throws and the whole copy fails for affected documents
samples.evidence: `snapshotJsonRoot` does a bare `JSON.parse(doc.toJSON())`. The docstring claims "same handling as scripts/copy-yorkie-documents.ts", but that script explicitly wraps the same call in a try/catch because "Some documents contain control characters that Yorkie's raw JSON string path does not escape correctly" (packages/backend/scripts/copy-yorkie-documents.ts:316-327, with `escapeControlCharsInJson` and a `detachYorkieValue` fallback). Without those fallbacks a sheet/slides/board root containing a control character makes the copy throw a SyntaxError, rolling the copy back and surfacing a 500 to the user.

samples.summary: Copying a never-opened `doc` document seeds a Tree with zero blocks, producing a document the docs editor cannot safely edit
samples.evidence: The JSON arm explicitly skips writing when the source root is empty (line 184-187) so the editor can seed it on first open, but the `doc` arm has no such guard: `readDocsRoot` returns `{ blocks: [] }` for a source that was never attached (docs-tree.ts:427-431), and `writeDocsRoot` then creates `new Tree({ type: 'doc', children: [] })` (docs-tree.ts:524-528). Because `content` now exists, the frontend's seeding paths are bypassed — `initialDocsRoot()`'s initialRoot only applies to a fresh key, and `ensureTree` in packages/frontend/src/app/docs/docs-view.tsx:52-58 returns early when `root.content` is a Tree. A docs tree with no block is the known crash mode (`Block not found`, see docs/tasks/archive/2026/05/20260505-undo-destroys-initial-block-todo.md:12). Also loses the `comments` container the editor seeds at bootstrap, re-introducing the LWW first-comment race described in packages/frontend/src/types/docs-document.ts:41-45.

samples.summary: CopySource is URL-encoded whole, percent-encoding the bucket/key separator
samples.evidence: `encodeURIComponent(`${this.bucket}/${this.storageKey(id)}`)` turns every `/` into `%2F`, including the bucket/key separator and any separator introduced by a configured storage prefix. S3/MinIO do unescape the header, but the AWS contract is that only the key components are URL-encoded; a deployment whose gateway does not unescape (or double-unescapes) would resolve the wrong source key and the copy would fail or copy the wrong object. Encoding the key path segments while leaving the separators literal is the safer form.

samples.summary: Content-copy rollback deletes the DB row but leaves the target Yorkie document created (and possibly partially written) on the server
samples.evidence: When `copyContent` throws, the row is deleted (lines 99-105) but nothing detaches/removes the Yorkie document at `<prefix><created.id>` that `withDocument` already created by attaching. If a later document happens to reuse that id (or a retried copy is issued), an orphan CRDT doc with partial content remains on the Yorkie server with no row referencing it.

samples.summary: Bulk copy aborts at the first failure and reports a generic error without saying which documents were copied
samples.evidence: `mutationFn: async ({ ids }) => { for (const id of ids) await copyDocument(id); }` — the first rejection breaks the loop, so the remaining ids are never attempted, and `onError: () => toast.error("Failed to copy")` gives the user no indication that some copies succeeded and which ids were skipped. The list does refetch on settled, but a partially-completed bulk action silently drops the rest.

verdict.reason: The claimed code is present and reachable exactly as described. document-copy.service.ts:176-198 snapshots the entire Yorkie root for sheet/slides/board and assigns every root key onto the copy with no filtering (only an empty-root early return at line 187). Sheet comment threads are stored inside that root: worksheet-document.ts:94-96 declares `comments` on Worksheet and line 147 seeds it, yorkie-worksheet-comments.ts:3-5,80 writes threads into `ws.comments`, and document-detail.tsx:241-248 reads `docRoot.sheets[...].comments`. Threads embed author userId/username/photo (sheets/src/comment/types.ts:29-36). This directly contradicts the invariant asserted in the class docstring (document-copy.service.ts:34-37) and docs/design/document-copy.md:33-35, and diverges from the `doc` arm, which rebuilds only from `root.content` (docs-tree.ts:427-432). No guard, filter, or caller-side sanitization exists (copy() invokes copyContent directly at line 93). Copied collaboration state that the code documents as never carried over is a broken invariant / incorrect state propagation in the correctness lane, so no refutation ground applies.

finding.summary: Snapshot round-trip demotes Yorkie Long values to 32-bit Integers, corrupting timestamps in copied roots
finding.evidence: The JSON arm writes `root[key] = value` with values that came out of `JSON.parse`, i.e. plain JS numbers. The repo documents that Yorkie 0.7.x stores any integer-valued JS number as a 32-bit Integer, which is why comment timestamps are written as bigint (`BigInt(ms) as unknown as number`) in packages/frontend/src/app/spreadsheet/yorkie-worksheet-comments.ts:8-14. Copying a sheet root therefore writes `createdAt` (~1.78e12) back as a plain number, truncating it to its low 32 bits — the copy's comment/any Long field decodes as a 1970 date. `scripts/copy-yorkie-documents.ts:115-118` (the cited precedent) has an explicit bigint branch; this implementation has none.

verdict.reason: The JSON-root arm of the copy is present exactly as described: document-copy.service.ts:179-198 snapshots the source root via snapshotJsonRoot (JSON.parse(doc.toJSON()), lines 209-220) and re-assigns each key with `(root as JsonRoot)[key] = value`, with no bigint/Long branch. The repo itself documents that @yorkie-js/sdk 0.7.x (pinned 0.7.14 in packages/backend/package.json:42) stores any integer-valued JS number as a 32-bit Integer and truncates ~1.78e12 timestamps, which is why comment timestamps are written as BigInt in yorkie-worksheet-comments.ts:8-14 and read back via fromYorkieMs. Those Long timestamps live inside the sheet root being snapshotted (worksheet-document.ts:94-96,147; toYorkieMs writes at yorkie-worksheet-comments.ts:65,74,79,90,105,139), so copying a sheet that has comment threads writes createdAt/editedAt/resolvedAt back as plain numbers and they decode as 1970 dates in the copy. No guard prevents this: copyContent is invoked unconditionally from copy() (line 93) and the only early return is the empty-root check (line 187); grep found no bigint/Long handling anywhere in packages/backend/src. The only inaccuracy in the finding is cosmetic — scripts/copy-yorkie-documents.ts:110-118 does have a bigint branch but it also converts to Number and is only a third-tier fallback — which does not refute the defect. Silent timestamp corruption on a real user path ("Make a copy" of a commented sheet) is a Correctness-lane data-integrity bug, so none of not-present/already-guarded/out-of-scope applies.

finding.summary: snapshotJsonRoot has no control-character fallback, so `JSON.parse(doc.toJSON())` throws and the whole copy fails for affected documents
finding.evidence: `snapshotJsonRoot` does a bare `JSON.parse(doc.toJSON())`. The docstring claims "same handling as scripts/copy-yorkie-documents.ts", but that script explicitly wraps the same call in a try/catch because "Some documents contain control characters that Yorkie's raw JSON string path does not escape correctly" (packages/backend/scripts/copy-yorkie-documents.ts:316-327, with `escapeControlCharsInJson` and a `detachYorkieValue` fallback). Without those fallbacks a sheet/slides/board root containing a control character makes the copy throw a SyntaxError, rolling the copy back and surfacing a 500 to the user.

verdict.reason: Verified exactly as described. `snapshotJsonRoot` (document-copy.service.ts:209-220) performs a bare `JSON.parse(doc.toJSON())` at line 212 plus a bare `JSON.parse(value)` unwrap loop at line 214, with no try/catch and no control-character escaping — despite the docstring at line 206 claiming "same handling as scripts/copy-yorkie-documents.ts". That script does NOT do the same thing: copy-yorkie-documents.ts:313-328 wraps the identical call in nested try/catch with the comment "Some documents contain control characters that Yorkie's raw JSON string path does not escape correctly", falling back to `JSON.stringify(getRoot())` then `detachYorkieValue(getRoot())`; it also routes every parse through `parseJsonSnapshot` (:81-94), which catches SyntaxErrors mentioning "control character" and retries via `escapeControlCharsInJson` (:18-79). The same hardening is independently duplicated in migrate-yorkie-worksheet-shape.ts:29,103,300-307 — two first-party scripts in this repo both needed it against real Yorkie sheet data, so the failure mode is empirically observed, not hypothetical. The path is live: snapshotJsonRoot is invoked at document-copy.service.ts:181 for every sheet/slides/board type (JSON_ROOT_TYPES :27, gate :176), and a thrown SyntaxError propagates into the catch at :94-108, which deletes the newly created document and rethrows at :107, surfacing a 500 and failing "Make a copy". No upstream guard sanitizes the root, and the specs (document-copy.service.spec.ts:179-192) cover only clean JSON, double-encoded JSON, and the non-object throw — no control-character case. Missing-guard crash breaking a core flow: in-lane and blocking.

finding.summary: Copying a never-opened `doc` document seeds a Tree with zero blocks, producing a document the docs editor cannot safely edit
finding.evidence: The JSON arm explicitly skips writing when the source root is empty (line 184-187) so the editor can seed it on first open, but the `doc` arm has no such guard: `readDocsRoot` returns `{ blocks: [] }` for a source that was never attached (docs-tree.ts:427-431), and `writeDocsRoot` then creates `new Tree({ type: 'doc', children: [] })` (docs-tree.ts:524-528). Because `content` now exists, the frontend's seeding paths are bypassed — `initialDocsRoot()`'s initialRoot only applies to a fresh key, and `ensureTree` in packages/frontend/src/app/docs/docs-view.tsx:52-58 returns early when `root.content` is a Tree. A docs tree with no block is the known crash mode (`Block not found`, see docs/tasks/archive/2026/05/20260505-undo-destroys-initial-block-todo.md:12). Also loses the `comments` container the editor seeds at bootstrap, re-introducing the LWW first-comment race described in packages/frontend/src/types/docs-document.ts:41-45.

verdict.reason: The code is present as described (doc arm writes an empty Tree when the source was never attached), but the claimed consequence is already guarded. The docs editor's `initialize()` seeds a paragraph block based on block count, not Tree presence: packages/docs/src/view/editor.ts:904-908 runs `if (docStore.getDocument().blocks.length === 0) docStore.setDocument(Doc.create().document)` before constructing `Doc` or any layout. docs-view.tsx:322-325 hands the live `YorkieDocStore` to `initialize`, `YorkieDocStore.getDocument()` (yorkie-doc-store.ts:544-556) reports `blocks: []` for the empty Tree, and `writeFullDocument` (yorkie-doc-store.ts:2695-2707) handles `childCount === 0` by skipping the delete and inserting children — so the copy is seeded, persisted, and editable on first open. The cited "Block not found" crash mode is specifically the case where `setDocument` is SKIPPED so `undoFloor` stays 0 (docs/tasks/archive/2026/05/20260505-undo-destroys-initial-block-todo.md:26-37); here `setDocument` runs and records `undoFloor` (yorkie-doc-store.ts:729-732), with the constructor recording it as well (line 529). The comments-container half is an explicitly documented, accepted fallback at yorkie-comment-store.ts:170-177 (`if (!root.comments) root.comments = {}`), the same state all legacy docs are in per docs-document.ts:13-14 — narrow and non-blocking, not data loss on the copy path. No content is lost either: the source truly had zero blocks.
